clue.text: Little ménage à trois?

parts.note: French for 'for three', giving the prefix meaning three
read loosely as an affair or brief liaison, a fling

explanation.surface: A wry question whether a three-person household arrangement counts as a small matter.
explanation.walkthrough: A ménage à trois is a three-way affair: a TRI-FLING, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifling means trivial or of small importance, a synonym of little in that sense.

clue.text: Idiot to assess how to measure strength

parts.note: a tit is British slang for a fool
to rate something is to judge or assess it

explanation.surface: A fool is asked how to gauge the strength of something.
explanation.walkthrough: TIT is British slang for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Titration is the chemist's method for finding the concentration of a solution by adding a reagent.

clue.text: First hot month move urinal outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go outside, around the month
move tells us the letters of urinal are moved into a new order

parts.note: August is the hottest month of the northern summer, AUG for short

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to relocate a urinal outdoors in the first hot month of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' looks like IN, but it belongs with month; the urinal's letters wrap round the month's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural event or speech is the opening one, so it is the first.

clue.text: Can you be under the table in this state? Yes and no

definitions.text: Can you be under the table in this state
definitions.meaning: under the table is slang for very drunk, a state also called by the answer
yes, a drunk can end up under the table; no, a table in this state has no supports to be under

explanation.walkthrough: Legless is British slang for extremely drunk; read literally it describes a table without legs, which nobody could get under.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for very drunk, the condition of someone who has slid under the table.

clue.text: Murky things blend in with this, ultimately

definitions.text: Murky things blend in with this, ultimately

indicators.note: murky suggests things muddled and unclear, so the letters are jumbled
ultimately points to the final letter of the word this

explanation.surface: With this condition, dim shapes merge into their surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the condition: to someone with it, things in the murk blend in.
explanation.definitionFit: Night blindness is poor vision in dim light, so dark objects merge into the background.

clue.text: Maintenance in this country initially poised to go backwards

indicators.note: in places the opening letter of poised inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: the setter is British, so this country is the UK

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of the word poised
backwards means the word for go is read from right to left

parts.note: go is a colloquial word for urinate, pee

explanation.surface: Something about maintenance in Britain being poised to go into reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is a euphemism for urinate, here PEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost or work of keeping something in good repair, its maintenance.

clue.text: Lock up and down

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to imprison or store securely
second meaning: to eat or drink something quickly

explanation.walkthrough: Up and down look like a pair of opposites, but they belong to two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to jail someone and, informally, to consume food or drink heartily.

clue.text: We'll cuddle regularly, duck

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the words We'll cuddle

explanation.surface: A promise of a cuddle, with a pet duck perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is a verb here, as in dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge or evade it, as to elude it.

clue.text: City set up incredible finish

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: mad can mean wild or unbelievable

explanation.surface: A city has arranged an unbelievable ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsdam is a German city near Berlin, site of the 1945 Allied conference.

clue.text: Financial agreement landlord cited for damage

parts.note: a letter is someone who lets property, a landlord

indicators.note: damage means the letters of cited for are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenant's deal mentions the landlord was taken to court over damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for damage' looks like the court case; only 'damage' is the signal, and 'cited for' supplies OFCREDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of credit is a bank's guarantee of payment in trade, a financial arrangement.

clue.text: Time partner acquires new accent

indicators.note: acquires means the partner takes the letter for new inside

parts.note: a WAG is the wife or girlfriend of a sports star

explanation.surface: A spouse picks up a fresh accent over time.
explanation.walkthrough: WAG is British tabloid shorthand for a footballer's wife or girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal or distinctive regional accent in speech.

clue.text: Older woman undressing to go along with a tease

indicators.note: undressing strips off the outer letters, leaving the inside of the word

parts.note: to go along with something is to agree

explanation.surface: An elderly lady undressing in order to tease someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go along' is not a link: go along is AGREE, stripped of its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-aunt is a parent's aunt, a woman from an older generation.

clue.text: Intensify conflict as unionist shifts left not right

indicators.note: the unionist's letter moves leftward to a new spot in the word
not tells us the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: U is an abbreviation for Unionist in Northern Irish politics

explanation.surface: A political row grows when a unionist changes sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The U of ARGUMENT moves one place to the left into the slot vacated by R.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment something is to increase or enlarge it, much as to intensify it.

clue.text: One with tousled blond mop sees openings for Tory's ousted wannabe leader

indicators.note: openings are the first letters of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A messy-haired blond politician is said to be the Conservative leader who was ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods at a famously tousled blond Tory leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A towhead is a person with very light, often unruly, flaxen hair.

clue.text: Feature of unlimited anxieties

indicators.note: without limits means losing both outer letters

explanation.surface: Boundless worry is described as a characteristic of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear is a feature of the face, one of its visible parts.

clue.text: Most of mystery lass's raving about love suggests masses involved in regular circulation

indicators.note: about places the letters around the zero for love
raving means wild and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
most of drops the final letter of the word mystery

parts.note: the lass, with the 's read as 'is' joining to raving
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A mysterious girl rants about love in a way that hints at planets orbiting.
explanation.walkthrough: lass's is read as 'lass is', so only LASS goes into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The solar system is the Sun with the planets and other bodies orbiting it on regular paths.

clue.text: Drunk upset facilities in Italy — he made a lot of hand gestures

definitions.text: he made a lot of hand gestures

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word for drunk upside down

parts.note: can is American slang for a toilet, the facilities

explanation.surface: A drunk upturns the toilets in Italy, waving his arms about.
explanation.walkthrough: Hand gestures describes a conductor at work; Toscanini was the great Italian conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini, the Italian conductor, directed orchestras through constant arm and hand movement.

clue.text: Remembering gorilla won, fellow runs

indicators.note: runs signals the letters run about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A gorilla's win in a race, a fellow running too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like R for runs in cricket, but here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowing for something means taking it into account, bearing it in mind.

clue.text: Poor sap is flabbergasted to be accepted as suitable

indicators.note: flabbergasted means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A pitiful fool is astonished to find himself accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means fitting or appropriate to the situation, a synonym of suitable.

clue.text: Elements of friction effect dissected by article

indicators.note: dissected by means the first word is cut open with the article placed inside

parts.note: wear is the effect of friction on a surface

explanation.surface: A scientific article analyses the effects of friction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elements of' reads as a phrase, but Elements alone is the definition: the elements are the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The elements is a term for the weather, especially wind and rain.

clue.text: Ripper takes another E to join in again

indicators.note: takes means the ripper holds the additional letter inside

parts.note: a renter is one who rends or tears, a ripper
a second letter E is added

explanation.surface: Jack the Ripper is pictured taking another victim.
explanation.walkthrough: Rend means tear, so a ripper is a RENTER in crossword terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to come back in or rejoin something after leaving it.

clue.text: British Embassy to offer asylum for Shamima, perhaps

indicators.note: offering asylum means sheltering it inside the words British Embassy

explanation.surface: A topical plea for the British Embassy to grant asylum to Shamima Begum.
explanation.walkthrough: Shamima Begum left Britain to join ISIS and was stripped of her citizenship; she is just an example of a woman here.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamima is a female name, so its bearer is referred to by the female pronoun.

clue.text: Patent it legally to protect label

indicators.note: the words patent it legally protect the answer by enclosing it

explanation.surface: Advice to obtain a patent legally to protect a brand.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle something is to give it a title or name, to label it.

clue.text: Judge drops order for suspension?

definitions.note: an exclamation, 'Refrain!', ordering someone to stop

parts.note: a referee is a judge in sport

explanation.surface: A judge abandons an order for someone's suspension.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a command: 'Refrain!' tells someone to suspend what they are doing.
explanation.definitionFit: Refrain as an imperative tells someone to hold back or stop an action.

clue.text: This person will tell a story to begin with

definitions.text: This person will tell a story
definitions.meaning: ... meaning: the ... person, as in a story narrated in the ... person by 'I'
second meaning: firstly, at the start

explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' means I or me, which grammar calls the first person, the narrator's voice in many stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the grammatical person of the narrating 'I' and also an adverb meaning at the outset.

clue.text: Respond to cover letter and legislate another time

indicators.note: the word for respond covers, wrapping around, the letter

parts.note: en is the printer's name for the letter N

explanation.surface: Instructions to answer a covering letter and pass a law again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover letter' reads as a phrase, but cover is the containment signal and letter is EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enact a law is to pass it into statute again.

clue.text: Got back up, reeling at first, to go after Dutch

indicators.note: back means the little word up is read in reverse
at first takes just the opening letter of the word reeling

parts.note: to chase is to go after

explanation.surface: Someone stood up again, reeling, to pursue the setter Dutch.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is the setter, but here he only stands for the abbreviation D.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchased means bought, and got is used for obtaining something in that sense.

clue.text: Fool around as last perversion

indicators.note: around means the word for fool goes round the other letter
last takes the final letter of the word as

explanation.surface: Someone jokes about a final perversion.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist can be a distortion or perversion of meaning or character.

clue.text: One in 15 go with it

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: A cryptic reference to joining in with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is SOLAR SYSTEM, of which this planet is one member.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun, a member of the solar system.

clue.text: Pointed laser kit in riot

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Laser equipment caught up in civil unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something starlike has radiating points, like a drawn star.
